question: Negotiations between the EU and the United States on the framework agreement regarding the exchange of personal data, including biometric data, for the purpose of screening and identity verification of travellers1, are expected to be concluded soon. According to the Commission, in this context ‘ensur[ing] respect of the EU’s standards on the protection of personal data’ is a ‘key priority’2.

This should not only be the case prior to signing an agreement, but also afterwards, in practice. The EU-US Umbrella Agreement, in force since 2017 and intended to improve the overall level of data protection in EU-US law enforcement cooperation, was supposed to be jointly reviewed by 2020. However, six years later, a joint review report has yet to be published. 1.

Why was no joint review of the EU-US Umbrella Agreement published, despite the legal requirement to do so3? If the data protection requirements of that agreement cannot be reviewed or assessed because there are no results to review, and noting the worrying developments in the US regarding the protection of personal data, how does the Commission expect EU citizens to have trust in the US authorities as regards the safety of their transferred biometric data?

Will the Commission ensure that the draft agreement fully incorporates the standards set by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) in relevant case law4, and if so, is it convinced that the envisaged agreement would hold up in court?

Also known as the Enhanced Border Security Partnership. https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/P-10-2026-000713-ASW_EN.html. 3 Article 23 of the EU-US Umbrella Agreement, (OJ L 336, 10.12.2016, p. 3–13 ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/agree_internation/2016/2220/oj). 4 In the field of (transatlantic) data exchange, including, but not limited to, the CJEU’s opinion on the envisaged EU-Canada PNR agreement and judgments in the Safe Harbour and Privacy Shield cases. 1 2
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.9.2026) The Commissioner for Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection updated the Honourable Members of the European Parliament in the Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs on 3 December 2025 about the review process. The information provided at the time continues to be valid.

In that meeting, the Commissioner for Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection referred to the ongoing review process for the EU-US umbrella agreement. The timing of the review has been affected by several factors, including shifting priorities during the COVID-19 pandemic and institutional changes on the US side following the change of Administration.

The exercise is also complex in nature, requiring gathering information on the relevant implementing policies and procedures in the US, the EU and its 27 Member States. The Commission looks forward to continuing to work with the US administration to conduct the joint review.

As regards the proposed framework agreement for the Enhanced Border Security Partnership1, it includes strong safeguards on data protection, in line with EU Law, including with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)2.
1 Proposal for a Council Decision on the signing and provisional application of a Framework Agreement

between the European Union and the United States of America on the reciprocal exchange of information for identity verification, and screening and vetting, relating to border procedures and applications for travel authorisations and visas, COM/2026/484 final, of 10 September 2026.

2 Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation) (Text with EEA relevance) OJ L 119, 4.5.2016, pp. 1–88.
